metric.unit: a SessionStart delivery of the beads context, in this project

properties.rule: The share of SessionStart beads deliveries whose command names bd-prime-hook.mjs is 1 over the 30 active days from the change, against 0 of the deliveries before it. A step at the change, not a rate, so the window is set by how many deliveries it takes to see the arm assignment hold -- 30 active days is about 318 at this projects 359 deliveries over 34 active days -- rather than by a power figure. THE NUMBER IS COUNTED FROM THE EMITTED command FIELD, NOT FROM THE HANDLERS OWN outcome: handlers/beads-delivery.yaml fires on every delivery it matches, so its base rate is 359 of 359 and asc handlers power says, verbatim, "nothing to plan -- the outcome was the same in all 359 units, so there is no variance for any effect size to move". Saying that here, before the grade, is the point of the property. That gap is what asc-09wx.8.3 (the replay) and asc-09wx.8.4 (sizes on events) exist to close.
properties.control: Other projects on this machine still run bd prime --hook-json (EV-55, Limitations) -- a real control, and one this project cannot read from its own store: it would have to be replayed over another projects transcripts.

properties.rule: Delivered units' 7-day rework rate is at least 30% lower, RELATIVELY, than held-out units' at 662 units (65 active days). Read git-side with EV-77's join and window: a unit counts as reworked when any source-bearing, window-closed commit in it is rewritten by a later commit within 7 days.
